# RBAC Groups

Copy page



cURL

##### [Create RBAC Group](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/create)

POST/v1/organizations/rbac_groups

Create an RBAC Group in the Claude Enterprise tenant. Groups created via the API have source type `"direct"`.

##### [List RBAC Groups](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/list)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_groups

List RBAC Groups in the Claude Enterprise tenant.

##### [Get RBAC Group](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/retrieve)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}

Retrieve an RBAC Group by ID.

##### [Update RBAC Group](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/update)

POST/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}

Update an RBAC Group's name. Groups provisioned by an identity provider (source type `"scim"`) cannot be modified via the API while an organization in the tenant uses SCIM provisioning.

##### [Delete RBAC Group](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/delete)

DELETE/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}

Delete an RBAC Group. Groups provisioned by an identity provider (source type `"scim"`) cannot be deleted via the API while an organization in the tenant uses SCIM provisioning.

##### Models



BetaRBACGroup object{ type: "rbac_group", id, created_at, 5 more }





RBACGroupDeleteResponse object{ type: "rbac_group_deleted", id }





type: "rbac_group_deleted"



Deleted object type.

For RBAC Groups, this is always `"rbac_group_deleted"`.

defaultrbac_group_deleted

id: string



ID of the RBAC Group.

#### RBAC Groups[Members](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members)

##### [List RBAC Group Members](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members/list)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}/members

List members of an RBAC Group.

##### [Add RBAC Group Member](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members/add)

POST/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}/members

Add a User to an RBAC Group. Membership of groups provisioned by an identity provider (source type `"scim"`) cannot be modified via the API while an organization in the tenant uses SCIM provisioning.

##### [Remove RBAC Group Member](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members/remove)

DELETE/v1/organizations/rbac_groups/{rbac_group_id}/members/{user_id}

Remove a User from an RBAC Group. Membership of groups provisioned by an identity provider (source type `"scim"`) cannot be modified via the API while an organization in the tenant uses SCIM provisioning.

# List RBAC Roles

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles

List RBAC Roles in the organization.

The RBAC Roles API is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Number of items to return per page.

Defaults to `20`. Ranges from `1` to `1000`.

default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Optionally set to the `next_page` token from the previous response.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaRBACRole](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles#beta_rbac_role) { type: "rbac_role", id, created_at, 3 more }





type: "rbac_role"



Object type.

For RBAC Roles, this is always `"rbac_role"`.

defaultrbac_role

id: string



ID of the RBAC Role.



created_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was created.

formatdate-time

display_name: string



Name of the RBAC Role. For a role created by Anthropic, this name can differ from the label claude.ai shows, and Anthropic may change the name. To keep a lasting reference to a role, store its `id`.



updated_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was last updated.

formatdate-time



name: string⁠Deprecated



Deprecated: use `display_name` instead. Name of the RBAC Role; always the same value as `display_name`.

Use \`display_name\` instead; \`name\` always has the same value.

has_more: boolean



Indicates whether there are more results beyond this page.

next_page: string or null



Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass as the `page` parameter on the next request.

List RBAC Roles

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/rbac_roles \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "rbac_role_016J8xVtKpDq3Wy9ZmN2hR4s",
      "created_at": "2024-10-30T23:58:27.427722Z",
      "display_name": "Project Editor",
      "name": "Project Editor",
      "type": "rbac_role",
      "updated_at": "2024-10-30T23:58:27.427722Z"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,

# List RBAC Role Permissions

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{rbac_role_id}/permissions

List the permissions an RBAC Role grants.

The RBAC Roles API is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only.

##### Path parameters

rbac_role_id: string



ID of the RBAC Role.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Number of items to return per page.

Defaults to `20`. Ranges from `1` to `1000`.

default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Optionally set to the `next_page` token from the previous response.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaRBACRolePermission](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions#beta_rbac_role_permission) { type: "rbac_role_permission", action, resource }





type: "rbac_role_permission"



Object type.

For RBAC Role Permissions, this is always `"rbac_role_permission"`.

defaultrbac_role_permission



action: string



Action the permission grants on the resource.

The vocabulary follows the resource: an `organization` grant carries a product-feature entitlement (for example `chat`), an admin-panel permission entitlement (`permission_*`), or a blanket capability-access mode — `capability_access_all` grants every product-feature entitlement, and `capability_access_all_ga` grants the generally-available subset as it stands at permission-check time; neither mode grants model-access entitlements. A consumer enumerating a role's per-feature grants should treat a blanket row as granting every product-feature entitlement it covers, or it will under-report the role's effective access. A `connector_tool` grant carries a tool-access action (`use` or `always_allow`); a `connector_scope` grant carries the scope action `grant` (the role may receive the named OAuth scope when tokens are minted for the connector); `connector` and `all_connectors` grants carry a tool-access action, the scope action, or an authentication-method action (`interactive` or `managed`).



resource: [BetaRBACOrganizationPermissionResource](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions#beta_rbac_organization_permission_resource) or [BetaRBACConnectorToolPermissionResource](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions#beta_rbac_connector_tool_permission_resource) or [BetaRBACConnectorScopePermissionResource](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions#beta_rbac_connector_scope_permission_resource) or 2 more



What the permission applies to.

A tagged union: `type` names the kind of resource and determines which identifier fields are present.

One of the following:



BetaRBACOrganizationPermissionResource object{ type: "organization", organization_id }





type: "organization"



Kind of resource the permission applies to.

defaultorganization

organization_id: string



UUID of the organization the permission applies to.



BetaRBACConnectorToolPermissionResource object{ type: "connector_tool", connector_id, tool_name }





type: "connector_tool"



Kind of resource the permission applies to.

defaultconnector_tool

connector_id: string



ID of the connector the permission applies to.



tool_name: string



Published name of the connector tool the permission applies to.

When the published name contains characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` (or collides with a reserved form), it is server-encoded into a stable `{prefix}_{32-hex}` form — a shortened readable prefix of the name plus a hash — from which the published name is not recoverable.



BetaRBACConnectorScopePermissionResource object{ type: "connector_scope", connector_id, scope }





type: "connector_scope"



Kind of resource the permission applies to.

defaultconnector_scope

connector_id: string



ID of the connector the permission applies to.



scope: string



OAuth scope the permission names — the role may receive this scope when tokens are minted for the connector.

Subject to the same encoding rule as `tool_name`: a scope containing characters outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` (or colliding with a reserved form) appears server-encoded in a stable `{prefix}_{32-hex}` form. OAuth scopes routinely contain `:` and `/`, so most appear encoded.



BetaRBACConnectorPermissionResource object{ type: "connector", connector_id }





type: "connector"



Kind of resource the permission applies to.

defaultconnector

connector_id: string



ID of the connector the permission applies to.



BetaRBACAllConnectorsPermissionResource object{ type: "all_connectors" }





type: "all_connectors"



Kind of resource the permission applies to.

defaultall_connectors

has_more: boolean



Indicates whether there are more results beyond this page.

next_page: string or null



Opaque cursor for the next page. Pass as the `page` parameter on the next request.

List RBAC Role Permissions

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/$RBAC_ROLE_ID/permissions \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "data": [
    {
      "action": "use",
      "resource": {
        "organization_id": "3c4f5e6d-7a8b-49c0-9d1e-2f3a4b5c6d7e",
        "type": "organization"
      },
      "type": "rbac_role_permission"
    }
  ],
  "has_more": true,
  "next_page": "eyJjdXJzb3IiOiAicmJhY19yb2xlXzAxIn0"
}
```

# Get RBAC Role

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{rbac_role_id}

Retrieve an RBAC Role by ID.

The RBAC Roles API is available to Claude Enterprise organizations only.

##### Path parameters

rbac_role_id: string



ID of the RBAC Role.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



BetaRBACRole object{ type: "rbac_role", id, created_at, 3 more }





type: "rbac_role"



Object type.

For RBAC Roles, this is always `"rbac_role"`.

defaultrbac_role

id: string



ID of the RBAC Role.



created_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was created.

formatdate-time

display_name: string



Name of the RBAC Role. For a role created by Anthropic, this name can differ from the label claude.ai shows, and Anthropic may change the name. To keep a lasting reference to a role, store its `id`.



updated_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was last updated.

formatdate-time



name: string⁠Deprecated



Deprecated: use `display_name` instead. Name of the RBAC Role; always the same value as `display_name`.

Use \`display_name\` instead; \`name\` always has the same value.

Get RBAC Role

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/$RBAC_ROLE_ID \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



{
  "id": "rbac_role_016J8xVtKpDq3Wy9ZmN2hR4s",
  "created_at": "2024-10-30T23:58:27.427722Z",
  "display_name": "Project Editor",
  "name": "Project Editor",
  "type": "rbac_role",
  "updated_at": "2024-10-30T23:58:27.427722Z"

```

# RBAC Roles

Copy page



cURL

##### [List RBAC Roles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/list)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles

List RBAC Roles in the organization.

##### [Get RBAC Role](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/retrieve)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{rbac_role_id}

Retrieve an RBAC Role by ID.

##### Models



BetaRBACRole object{ type: "rbac_role", id, created_at, 3 more }





type: "rbac_role"



Object type.

For RBAC Roles, this is always `"rbac_role"`.

defaultrbac_role

id: string



ID of the RBAC Role.



created_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was created.

formatdate-time

display_name: string



Name of the RBAC Role. For a role created by Anthropic, this name can differ from the label claude.ai shows, and Anthropic may change the name. To keep a lasting reference to a role, store its `id`.



updated_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime string indicating when the RBAC Role was last updated.

formatdate-time



name: string⁠Deprecated



Deprecated: use `display_name` instead. Name of the RBAC Role; always the same value as `display_name`.

Use \`display_name\` instead; \`name\` always has the same value.

#### RBAC Roles[Permissions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions)

##### [List RBAC Role Permissions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/rbac_roles/permissions/list)

GET/v1/organizations/rbac_roles/{rbac_role_id}/permissions

List the permissions an RBAC Role grants.

# Get Current Organization

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/me

Retrieve information about the organization associated with the authenticated API key.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



BetaOrganization object{ type: "organization", id, name }





type: "organization"



Object type.

For Organizations, this is always `"organization"`.

defaultorganization



id: string



ID of the Organization.

formatuuid

name: string



Name of the Organization.

Get Current Organization

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/me \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "id": "12345678-1234-5678-1234-567812345678",
  "name": "Organization Name",
  "type": "organization"
}
```

# Archive Service Account

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/service_accounts/{service_account_id}/archive

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

Archive a service account.

Idempotent; re-archiving returns the service account with its original `archived_at`. Rejected with 400 if any live (non-archived) federation rule still targets this service account, same as issuer archival; archive those rules first or change their target to another service account.

##### Path parameters

service_account_id: string



ID of the service account to archive.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



Optional header to specify the beta version(s) you want to use.

One of the following:

string

cURL

POST/v1/organizations/service_accounts

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

Create a service account.

A service account is a named workload identity that federation rules target. `organization_role` is `developer` (default) or `admin`; a rule may only be created or retargeted to grant `org:admin` scope when the target's `organization_role` is `admin`. Creating an `admin`-role service account requires an interactive credential (a user OAuth token or a Console session) — a workload may only create `developer`-role service accounts.

# List Service Accounts

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/service_accounts

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

List service accounts in the caller's organization.

Results are ordered by creation time, newest first. Use `limit` and the `next_page` cursor to paginate; set `include_archived=true` to include archived service accounts.

##### Query parameters



include_archived: optional boolean



defaultfalse



limit: optional number



Number of results per page.

default20

minimum1

maximum100

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page`.

# Update Service Account

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/service_accounts/{service_account_id}

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

Update a service account.

Only `description` and `organization_role` are mutable; `name` cannot be changed. Archived service accounts cannot be updated; this returns 400. Setting `organization_role` to `admin` (even when unchanged) requires an interactive credential (a user OAuth token or a Console session).

##### Path parameters

service_account_id: string



ID of the service account to update.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



Optional header to specify the beta version(s) you want to use.

One of the following:

string

# Add Workspace To Service Account

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/service_accounts/{service_account_id}/workspaces

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

Add a service account to a workspace with the given `workspace_role`.

Mirror of `POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/service_accounts`, addressed from the service-account side; both create the same membership. If the service account is already an explicit member of the workspace, its `workspace_role` is replaced with the value supplied here. Archived workspaces return 400. Archived service accounts cannot be added and are rejected.

##### Path parameters

service_account_id: string



ID of the service account.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



Optional header to specify the beta version(s) you want to use.

One of the following:

string





"prompt-caching-2024-07-31"





workspace_role: [BetaNoBillingWorkspaceRole](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/workspaces#beta_no_billing_workspace_role)



##### Returns



BetaServiceAccountWorkspaceMember object{ type: "service_account_workspace_member", created_by_actor_id, implicit, 3 more }





type: "service_account_workspace_member"



defaultservice_account_workspace_member

created_by_actor_id: string or null



Tagged ID (`user_...`/`svac_...`) of the actor who created this membership.

implicit: boolean or null



True when this is the implicit default-workspace membership every service account has when no explicit membership exists. Implicit memberships have role `workspace_user` and cannot be removed.

service_account_id: string

# List Workspaces For Service Account

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/service_accounts/{service_account_id}/workspaces

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

List the workspaces a service account is a member of.

Each entry includes the service account's `workspace_role` in that workspace. Use `limit` and the `next_page` cursor to paginate. When the service account has no explicit default-workspace membership, the implicit (`implicit: true`) membership is returned as the first entry on the first page; with `limit=1` the first page may return up to 2 entries (the implicit entry plus one explicit membership) so a pagination cursor can be derived. Memberships are returned only while the service account is active. Without a `page` cursor, an archived service account returns an empty list. A `page` cursor that does not match an active membership returns a 400 invalid-request error. A cursor stops matching when the membership is removed, the workspace is deleted, or the service account is archived. Restart pagination from the first page to recover.

##### Path parameters

service_account_id: string



ID of the service account.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Number of results per page.

default20

minimum1

maximum100

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page`.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)

# Remove Workspace From Service Account

Copy page



cURL

DELETE/v1/organizations/service_accounts/{service_account_id}/workspaces/{workspace_id}

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

Remove a service account from a workspace.

Mirror of `DELETE /workspaces/{workspace_id}/service_accounts/{service_account_id}`, addressed from the service-account side. Removal is idempotent (returns 200 even if the membership was already removed). A DELETE against the implicit default-workspace membership returns 200 but is a no-op and the membership persists; deleting an explicit default-workspace row reverts to the implicit `workspace_user` membership. Archived workspaces return 400.

##### Path parameters

service_account_id: string



ID of the service account.

workspace_id: string



ID of the workspace.

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

**Requires an OAuth access token with the `org:admin` scope**, from `ant auth login --scope org:admin` or a workload identity federation rule; Admin API keys are not accepted. See [Manage WIF with the Admin API](../Other/manage-claude-wif-admin-api.md).

A service account is a pure identity: name + org. Authorization lives on whatever references it (federation rules).

implicit: boolean or null



True when this is the implicit default-workspace membership every service account has when no explicit membership exists. Implicit memberships have role `workspace_user` and cannot be removed.



Tagged workspace ID (`wrkspc_...`).



Role of the service account in this workspace. Service accounts cannot hold the `workspace_billing` role.

One of the following:

"workspace_admin"





"workspace_restricted_developer"

# Set Spend Limit

POST/v1/organizations/spend_limits

Set a spend limit.

Upsert keyed on (scope, period): setting a limit that already exists overwrites it in place. A Claude Enterprise organization sets `user` limits. Its seat-tier, group, and organization-level defaults are configured in claude.ai. A Claude Console organization sets `organization` and `workspace` limits, which are monthly and always carry an amount. Setting those limits is in an early access preview. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

##### Body

amount: string or null



Limit amount as a non-negative integer decimal string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency (cents for USD): "50000" is \$500.00. `null` sets an explicit no-limit override for this scope and `period` only — each period resolves independently, so caps for other periods still apply.



scope: User or Organization or Workspace



What the limit applies to. Claude Enterprise organizations set `user` limits. Claude Console organizations set `organization` and `workspace` limits. Any other combination returns 400. Setting `organization` and `workspace` limits through the API is in an early access preview. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

One of the following:



User object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



Organization object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization



Workspace object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.



period: optional "daily" or "monthly" or "weekly"



One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"



##### Returns



BetaSpendLimit object{ type: "spend_limit", id, amount, 5 more }



A configured spend limit: a cap on metered spend for one scope and period.

Set Spend Limit

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "amount": "50000",
          "scope": {
            "type": "user",
            "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"
          },
          "period": "monthly"
        }'
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "id": "id",
  "amount": "50000",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "currency": "USD",
  "period": "monthly",
  "scope": {
    "type": "user",
    "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"
  },
  "type": "spend_limit",
  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
}
```

##### Returns Examples

Response 200



```python
{
  "id": "id",
  "amount": "50000",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "currency": "USD",
  "period": "monthly",
  "scope": {
    "type": "user",
    "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"
  },
  "type": "spend_limit",
  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"

# Delete Spend Limit

Copy page



cURL

DELETE/v1/organizations/spend_limits/{spend_limit_id}

Delete a spend limit.

For a Claude Enterprise organization, this deletes a per-user override, and the member falls back to any inherited spend limit at that period. Its seat-tier, group, and organization-level rows cannot be deleted via this endpoint. A Claude Console organization deletes its organization and workspace limits, but not its `usage_tier` limit. Deleting organization and workspace limits through the API is in an early access preview.

##### Path parameters

spend_limit_id: string



ID of the Spend Limit.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



type: "spend_limit_deleted"



defaultspend_limit_deleted

id: string



Delete Spend Limit

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits/$SPEND_LIMIT_ID \
    -X DELETE \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

---

# List Effective Spend Limits

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective

List each member's effective spend limit and period-to-date spend.

Returns one row per (member, period) the member resolves a spend limit for, with the `source` scope the spend limit was inherited from. Paginates by member, so a member's periods never split across pages. Supported for Claude Enterprise organizations only, not for Claude Console organizations.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Maximum number of members per page. A member's period rows never split across pages, so a page may carry more rows than this. Defaults to `20`.

default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page` field.



period: optional array of "daily" or "monthly" or "weekly"



Restrict the report to these limit periods. Omit to return one row per period each member resolves a spend limit for.

maxItems3

One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"





user_ids: optional array of string



Restrict the report to these members, by tagged user ID (`user_...`). At most 100 entries.

maxItems100

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaSpendSummary](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_summary) { actor, amount, currency, 5 more }





actor: [BetaSpendLimitUserActor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_actor) or [BetaSpendLimitScopedAPIKeyActor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_scoped_api_key_actor)



One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserActor object{ type: "user_actor", deleted, email_address, 2 more }



A user within the organization. `name` and `email_address` are null when the underlying account is unavailable or has been deleted; `deleted` is true only for deleted accounts.



type: "user_actor"



Actor type. Always `user_actor`.

defaultuser_actor



deleted: boolean



True only when the underlying account has been deleted.

defaultfalse

email_address: string or null



The user's email address. Null when the account is unavailable or has been deleted.

name: string or null



The user's current display name. Null when the account is unavailable, has been deleted, or has no name set.

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the user.



BetaSpendLimitScopedAPIKeyActor object{ type: "scoped_api_key_actor", scoped_api_key_id }



A scoped Admin API key acting on behalf of the organization.



type: "scoped_api_key_actor"



defaultscoped_api_key_actor

scoped_api_key_id: string



amount: string or null



Effective limit amount as a non-negative integer decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD). `null` means no limit applies for this row's `period` — each period resolves independently, so another period may still cap this member.

currency: string



ISO 4217 code of the organization's billing currency; the unit for `amount` and `period_to_date_spend`.



period: [BetaSpendLimitPeriod](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_period)



Period this row's effective limit and spend are reported for.

One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"



period_to_date_spend: string



The member's spend so far in the current period, as a non-negative decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD). May carry fractional minor units up to three decimal places (e.g. `"12050.5"`) — metered usage is not rounded to whole cents. Reads as `"0"` when the spend reading is temporarily unavailable.



scope: [BetaSpendLimitUserScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitSeatTierScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_seat_tier_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitRBACGroupScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_rbac_group_scope) or 4 more



One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserScope object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



BetaSpendLimitSeatTierScope object{ type: "seat_tier", seat_tier }





type: "seat_tier"



defaultseat_tier

seat_tier: string





BetaSpendLimitRBACGroupScope object{ type: "rbac_group", rbac_group_id }





type: "rbac_group"



defaultrbac_group

rbac_group_id: string





BetaSpendLimitOrganizationServiceScope object{ type: "organization_service", service }





type: "organization_service"



defaultorganization_service

service: string





BetaSpendLimitOrganizationScope object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization



BetaSpendLimitWorkspaceScope object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.



BetaSpendLimitUsageTierScope object{ type: "usage_tier" }



Scope of the monthly spend cap Anthropic sets for a Claude Console organization from its usage tier, or a higher cap Anthropic granted the organization. Read-only; its `created_at` and `updated_at` are the organization's creation time, so `amount` can change while `updated_at` stays the same.



type: "usage_tier"



Scope type. Always `usage_tier` for this scope.

defaultusage_tier



source: [BetaSpendLimitUserScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitSeatTierScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_seat_tier_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitRBACGroupScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_rbac_group_scope) or 4 more



One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserScope object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"

# Approve Spend Limit Increase Request

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{spend_limit_increase_request_id}/approve

Approve a pending spend limit increase request.

Writes a per-user spend limit at `amount` for the requester and transitions the request to `approved`. `period` defaults to the period the member was blocked on. Anthropic emails the requester unless `suppress_notification` is set.

##### Path parameters

spend_limit_increase_request_id: string



ID of the spend limit increase request.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Body

amount: string



New per-user spend limit as a non-negative integer decimal string (minor units).



period: optional [BetaSpendLimitPeriod](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_period) or null



One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"



suppress_notification: optional boolean



##### Returns



type: "spend_limit_increase_request"



defaultspend_limit_increase_request

id: string





actor: [BetaSpendLimitUserActor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_actor) or [BetaSpendLimitScopedAPIKeyActor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_scoped_api_key_actor)



One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserActor object{ type: "user_actor", deleted, email_address, 2 more }



A user within the organization. `name` and `email_address` are null when the underlying account is unavailable or has been deleted; `deleted` is true only for deleted accounts.



type: "user_actor"



Actor type. Always `user_actor`.

defaultuser_actor



deleted: boolean



True only when the underlying account has been deleted.

defaultfalse

email_address: string or null



The user's email address. Null when the account is unavailable or has been deleted.

name: string or null



The user's current display name. Null when the account is unavailable, has been deleted, or has no name set.

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the user.



BetaSpendLimitScopedAPIKeyActor object{ type: "scoped_api_key_actor", scoped_api_key_id }



"daily"



"monthly"

"weekly"

resolved_at: string or null



formatdate-time



One of the following:

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/$SPEND_LIMIT_INCREASE_REQUEST_ID/approve \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "amount": "50000",
          "period": "monthly"
        }'
```

# Deny Spend Limit Increase Request

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/{spend_limit_increase_request_id}/deny

Deny a pending spend limit increase request.

Idempotent on `denied`; denying an already-`approved` request returns 400. Anthropic emails the requester unless `suppress_notification` is set.

##### Path parameters

spend_limit_increase_request_id: string



ID of the spend limit increase request.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).

##### Body

suppress_notification: optional boolean



##### Returns



BetaSpendLimitIncreaseRequest object{ type: "spend_limit_increase_request", id, actor, 6 more }



Deny Spend Limit Increase Request

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests/$SPEND_LIMIT_INCREASE_REQUEST_ID/deny \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
    -d '{}'
```

GET/v1/organizations/spend_limit_increase_requests

List spend limit increase requests, most recent first.

Pending requests include a live `spend_summary` for the requester. Requests whose requester is no longer a member are excluded.

##### Query parameters

actor_ids: optional array of string



Filter by requester, as `user_...` tagged IDs.



limit: optional number



default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page`.



status: optional array of [BetaSpendLimitIncreaseRequestStatus](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits/increase_requests#beta_spend_limit_increase_request_status)



Filter by status. Omit to return all.

One of the following:

"approved"



"denied"



"pending"



##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



# List Effective Spend Limits

GET/v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective

List each member's effective spend limit and period-to-date spend.

Returns one row per (member, period) the member resolves a spend limit for, with the `source` scope the spend limit was inherited from. Paginates by member, so a member's periods never split across pages.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Maximum number of members per page. A member's period rows never split across pages, so a page may carry more rows than this. Defaults to `20`.

default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page` field.



period: optional array of "daily" or "monthly" or "weekly"



Restrict the report to these limit periods. Omit to return one row per period each member resolves a spend limit for.

maxItems3

One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"





user_ids: optional array of string



Restrict the report to these members, by tagged user ID (`user_...`). At most 100 entries.

maxItems100

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaSpendSummary](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_summary) { actor, amount, currency, 5 more }





actor: UserActor or ScopedAPIKeyActor



One of the following:



UserActor object{ type: "user_actor", deleted, email_address, 2 more }



A user within the organization. `name` and `email_address` are null when the underlying account is unavailable or has been deleted; `deleted` is true only for deleted accounts.



type: "user_actor"



Actor type. Always `user_actor`.

defaultuser_actor



deleted: boolean



True only when the underlying account has been deleted.

defaultfalse

email_address: string or null



The user's email address. Null when the account is unavailable or has been deleted.

name: string or null



The user's current display name. Null when the account is unavailable, has been deleted, or has no name set.

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the user.



ScopedAPIKeyActor object{ type: "scoped_api_key_actor", scoped_api_key_id }



A scoped Admin API key acting on behalf of the organization.



type: "scoped_api_key_actor"



defaultscoped_api_key_actor

scoped_api_key_id: string



amount: string or null



Effective limit amount as a non-negative integer decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD). `null` means no limit applies for this row's `period` — each period resolves independently, so another period may still cap this member.

currency: string



ISO 4217 code of the organization's billing currency; the unit for `amount` and `period_to_date_spend`.



period: "daily" or "monthly" or "weekly"



Period this row's effective limit and spend are reported for.

One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"



period_to_date_spend: string



The member's spend so far in the current period, as a non-negative decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD). May carry fractional minor units up to three decimal places (e.g. `"12050.5"`) — metered usage is not rounded to whole cents. Reads as `"0"` when the spend reading is temporarily unavailable.



scope: User or SeatTier or RBACGroup or 3 more



One of the following:



User object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



SeatTier object{ type: "seat_tier", seat_tier }





type: "seat_tier"



defaultseat_tier

seat_tier: string





RBACGroup object{ type: "rbac_group", rbac_group_id }





type: "rbac_group"



defaultrbac_group

rbac_group_id: string





OrganizationService object{ type: "organization_service", service }





type: "organization_service"



defaultorganization_service

service: string





Organization object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization



Workspace object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.



source: User or SeatTier or RBACGroup or 3 more



One of the following:



User object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



SeatTier object{ type: "seat_tier", seat_tier }





type: "seat_tier"



defaultseat_tier

seat_tier: string





RBACGroup object{ type: "rbac_group", rbac_group_id }





type: "rbac_group"



defaultrbac_group

rbac_group_id: string





OrganizationService object{ type: "organization_service", service }





type: "organization_service"



defaultorganization_service

service: string





Organization object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization

Workspace object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.

spend_limit_id: string



next_page: string or null

# List Spend Limits

Copy page



cURL

GET/v1/organizations/spend_limits

List the organization's spend limits.

Limits are grouped by scope type, in the order `organization`, `seat_tier`, `rbac_group`, `organization_service`, `user`; within a type they come in a fixed order that is not creation order. Supported for Claude Enterprise organizations only, not for Claude Console organizations.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Maximum number of limits per page. Defaults to `20`.

default20

minimum1

maximum1000

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page` field.



scope_type: optional array of "organization" or "organization_service" or "rbac_group" or 3 more



Return only limits with these scope types. Omit for all.

maxItems100

One of the following:

"organization"



"organization_service"



"rbac_group"



"seat_tier"



"user"



"workspace"



##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `spend-limit-reads-2026-09-26` in this header.

One of the following:

string

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaSpendLimit](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit) { type: "spend_limit", id, amount, 6 more }





type: "spend_limit"



Object type. Always `spend_limit`.

defaultspend_limit

id: string



Unique tagged ID of the spend limit (`spl_...`).

amount: string or null



Limit amount as a non-negative integer decimal string in the minor unit of `currency` (cents for USD): "50000" is \$500.00. `null` means no numeric cap is configured at this scope — see the effective report for whether a limit applies.



created_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime at which the spend limit was created.

formatdate-time

currency: string



ISO 4217 code of the organization's billing currency; the unit for `amount`.

is_enabled: boolean



Read-only. `false` when extra usage is switched off for this organization (`organization` limit); `amount` is kept and applies again when it's switched back on. Always `true` for other limits.



period: [BetaSpendLimitPeriod](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_period)



Length of the window the limit resets over. `amount` caps spend within each period.

One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"





scope: [BetaSpendLimitUserScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitSeatTierScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_seat_tier_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitRBACGroupScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_rbac_group_scope) or 4 more



What the limit applies to. A tagged union on `type`; each variant carries the identifier for its scope.

One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserScope object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



BetaSpendLimitSeatTierScope object{ type: "seat_tier", seat_tier }





type: "seat_tier"



defaultseat_tier

seat_tier: string





BetaSpendLimitRBACGroupScope object{ type: "rbac_group", rbac_group_id }





type: "rbac_group"



defaultrbac_group

rbac_group_id: string





BetaSpendLimitOrganizationServiceScope object{ type: "organization_service", service }





type: "organization_service"



defaultorganization_service

service: string





BetaSpendLimitOrganizationScope object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization



BetaSpendLimitWorkspaceScope object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.



BetaSpendLimitUsageTierScope object{ type: "usage_tier" }



Scope of the monthly spend cap Anthropic sets for a Claude Console organization from its usage tier, or a higher cap Anthropic granted the organization. Read-only; its `created_at` and `updated_at` are the organization's creation time, so `amount` can change while `updated_at` stays the same.



type: "usage_tier"



Scope type. Always `usage_tier` for this scope.

defaultusage_tier



updated_at: string



RFC 3339 datetime at which the spend limit was last modified.

formatdate-time

next_page: string or null



List Spend Limits

```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: spend-limit-reads-2026-09-26' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

{

      "id": "id",

      "scope": {
        "type": "user",
        "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"

# Set Spend Limit

Copy page



cURL

POST/v1/organizations/spend_limits

Set a spend limit.

Upsert keyed on (scope, period): setting a limit that already exists overwrites it in place. A Claude Enterprise organization sets `user` limits. Its seat-tier, group, and organization-level defaults are configured in claude.ai. A Claude Console organization sets `organization` and `workspace` limits, which are monthly and always carry an amount. Setting those limits is in an early access preview. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



Optional header to specify the beta version(s) you want to use.

One of the following:

string



"message-batches-2024-09-24"



"prompt-caching-2024-07-31"



"computer-use-2024-10-22"











"user-profiles-2026-03-24"



"user-profiles-2026-08-18"











"spend-limit-reads-2026-09-26"



"telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11"



##### Body

amount: string or null



Limit amount as a non-negative integer decimal string in the minor unit of the organization's billing currency (cents for USD): "50000" is \$500.00. `null` sets an explicit no-limit override for this scope and `period` only — each period resolves independently, so caps for other periods still apply.



scope: [BetaSpendLimitUserScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_user_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitOrganizationScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_organization_scope) or [BetaSpendLimitWorkspaceScope](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_workspace_scope)



What the limit applies to. Claude Enterprise organizations set `user` limits. Claude Console organizations set `organization` and `workspace` limits. Any other combination returns 400. Setting `organization` and `workspace` limits through the API is in an early access preview. To request access, contact your Anthropic account team.

One of the following:



BetaSpendLimitUserScope object{ type: "user", user_id }



Scope selecting a single member of the organization.



type: "user"



Scope type. Always `user` for this scope.

defaultuser

user_id: string



Tagged ID of the member the spend limit applies to.



BetaSpendLimitOrganizationScope object{ type: "organization" }





type: "organization"



defaultorganization



BetaSpendLimitWorkspaceScope object{ type: "workspace", workspace_id }



Scope selecting one workspace of a Claude Console organization.



type: "workspace"



Scope type. Always `workspace` for this scope.

defaultworkspace

workspace_id: string



Tagged ID of the workspace the spend limit applies to.



period: optional [BetaSpendLimitPeriod](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/spend_limits#beta_spend_limit_period)



One of the following:

"daily"



"monthly"



"weekly"



##### Returns



BetaSpendLimit object{ type: "spend_limit", id, amount, 6 more }



A configured spend limit: a cap on metered spend for one scope and period.

Set Spend Limit

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/spend_limits \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "amount": "50000",
          "scope": {
            "type": "user",
            "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"
          },
          "period": "monthly"
        }'
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "id": "id",
  "amount": "50000",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "currency": "USD",
  "is_enabled": true,
  "period": "daily",
  "scope": {
    "type": "user",
    "user_id": "user_01WCz1FkmYMm4gnmykNKUu3Q"
  },
  "type": "spend_limit",
  "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
}
```

##### Returns Examples



# Create a Telemetry Destination

Copy page



API version 2026-10-21

cURL

POST/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations

Register an OpenTelemetry destination for the organization.

The destination starts in state `enabled`. An organization can have at most 10 destinations, including disabled ones.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](../Other/manage-claude-opentelemetry.md#add-a-destination) to learn more about adding a destination.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header.

One of the following:

##### Body



endpoint_url: string



The base URL of your collector's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, for example `https://gateway.example.com`.

The URL must use `https` and a hostname, not an IP address. The port, if given, must be 443. The URL must not contain a query string, a fragment, or a username and password. At most 2,048 characters.

A path prefix, such as `/otlp`, is allowed. Don't include the per-signal path (`/v1/traces`), because the API appends it on delivery. If your collector takes traces on another path, also set `traces.endpoint_url`.

minLength1

maxLength2048



workspaces: [BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesParams](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_workspaces_params)



Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers.

One of the following:

display_name: optional string or null



Human-readable name for the destination. Optional. 1 to 255 characters.



headers: optional map\[string\]



Request headers that the API sends with every delivery, typically your collector's authentication header (for example `authorization`).

The API stores the values encrypted and never returns them. Reads show only `header_names`.

At most 20 headers. Names are at most 128 characters. Two names can't differ only in case. Values are printable ASCII, at most 4,096 characters, and can't begin or end with a space. Names and values together are at most 16,384 bytes.

Reserved names are rejected, for example `host`, `cookie`, `user-agent`, and names that start with `content-`, `proxy-`, `x-forwarded-`, or `anthropic-`. For this check, `_` in a name counts as `-`.



traces: optional [BetaTelemetryDestinationTracesParams](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_traces_params) { content_mode, enabled, endpoint_url, max_content_bytes }



The settings for the traces that the destination receives. If you leave it out, every setting takes its default.



content_mode: optional [BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_content_mode) or null



What the exported spans contain. Defaults to `metadata_only` on create.

On update, `null` sets `metadata_only`.

One of the following:

"metadata_only"



The spans contain identifiers, timing, status, token counts, and similar metadata. They don't contain prompt text, completion text, or tool inputs and outputs.



"content"



The spans contain the same metadata as `metadata_only`, plus message and tool content.

An organization with a data-handling restriction, such as under HIPAA, can't choose this mode. The API exports only metadata for such an organization, even to a destination that already has `content`.

enabled: optional boolean



Whether the destination receives traces. Defaults to true on create. It cannot be null.



endpoint_url: optional string or null



The full URL of your collector's traces endpoint, for a collector that takes traces on a path other than `/v1/traces`. The API posts traces to it exactly as given and appends nothing.

The same rules as for `endpoint_url` apply, except that any path is allowed. It must have the same scheme, host, and port as `endpoint_url`. At most 2,048 characters.

On create, `null` is the same as leaving it out. On update, `null` removes it. The API then posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended. A change of this URL alone keeps the registered headers.

maxLength2048



max_content_bytes: optional number or null



The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, from 1 up to the API's maximum. `null` sets no bound, so only the API's maximum applies.

On create, leaving it out is the same as `null`. The error for a value above the maximum states the maximum.

formatint32

##### Returns



BetaTelemetryDestination object{ type: "telemetry_destination", id, created_at, 8 more }



An OpenTelemetry destination: an OTLP/HTTP endpoint, the request headers sent with every delivery to it, what the exported spans contain, and which workspaces it covers. A destination belongs to an organization. A workspace's spans go to every enabled destination that covers it.

Create a Telemetry Destination

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2026-10-21' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
    -d '{
          "endpoint_url": "x",
          "workspaces": {
            "type": "all"
          }
        }'
```

Response 200



{
  "id": "id",
  "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
  "delivery_health": {
    "last_error": "last_error",

    "last_success_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
  },
  "display_name": "display_name",
  "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
  "header_names": [
    "string"
  ],
  "state": {
    "type": "enabled"
  },

    "content_mode": "metadata_only",
    "enabled": true,
    "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
    "max_content_bytes": 0
  },
  "type": "telemetry_destination",

  }

# Delete a Telemetry Destination

Copy page



API version 2026-10-21

cURL

DELETE/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/{destination_id}

Delete a destination and its workspace list.

The API stops sending spans to the destination. The spans of the workspaces it covered still go to the other destinations that cover them. A deleted destination can't be read, listed, or restored.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](../Other/manage-claude-opentelemetry.md#delivery-and-health) to learn more about managing a destination.

##### Path parameters

destination_id: string



ID of the destination (`tdst_...`).

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header.

One of the following:

string



"message-batches-2024-09-24"



"prompt-caching-2024-07-31"



"computer-use-2024-10-22"



"computer-use-2025-01-24"



"mcp-client-2025-11-20"



"dev-full-thinking-2025-05-14"

Delete a Telemetry Destination



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/$DESTINATION_ID \

    -H 'anthropic-version: 2026-10-21' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200

```python
{
  "id": "id",
  "type": "telemetry_destination_deleted"
}

# List Telemetry Destinations

Copy page



API version 2023-06-01

cURL

GET/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations

List the organization's destinations, newest first, optionally only those that cover given workspaces.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](../Other/manage-claude-opentelemetry.md#set-up-api-tracing) to learn more about destinations.

##### Query parameters



limit: optional number



Number of destinations to return per page, between 1 and 1,000. Defaults to 20.

formatint32

page: optional string



Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_page`. Leave it out to get the first page.



workspace_ids: optional array of string



Return only the destinations that cover at least one of these workspaces (`wrkspc_...`).

Send at most 100 IDs, as `workspace_ids[]`. A destination covers a workspace when its `workspaces.type` is `all`, when its `include` list has the workspace, or when its `exclude` list doesn't have it. Destinations in either state can match. An ID that isn't the ID of one of the organization's workspaces doesn't match any destination, not even one whose type is `all`.

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header.

One of the following:

string

##### Returns



data: array of [BetaTelemetryDestination](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination) { type: "telemetry_destination", id, created_at, 8 more }



Destinations on this page, newest first.

type: "telemetry_destination"



id: string



The unique ID of the destination (`tdst_...`).



created_at: string



Time the destination was created.

formatdate-time



delivery_health: [BetaTelemetryDestinationDeliveryHealth](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_delivery_health) { last_error, last_error_at, last_success_at }



The most recent delivery results for this destination.



last_error: string or null



A message that describes the most recent failed delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has failed yet.

Examples are `temporary DNS failure`, `TLS failure`, `timeout`, `connection failure`, `invalid address`, `HTTP error (status 503)`, and `redirect (status 301)`. The message is `invalid address` both for a hostname that doesn't exist and for an address that isn't publicly routable. It never contains the endpoint's response body, a header value, a network address, or TLS details.

`last_error` and `last_error_at` always change together. A later successful delivery doesn't clear them. If `last_success_at` is later than `last_error_at`, a delivery has succeeded since this failure.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](../Other/manage-claude-opentelemetry.md#delivery-errors) to learn the likely cause of each error.



last_error_at: string or null



Time of the failure that `last_error` describes. Changes together with `last_error`. Null until a delivery first fails.

formatdate-time



last_success_at: string or null



Time of the most recent successful delivery to the destination, or `null` if no delivery has succeeded yet.

formatdate-time

display_name: string or null



Human-readable name for the destination. Null when none was set.



endpoint_url: string



The base URL of the destination's OTLP/HTTP endpoint, exactly as registered.

The API appends the per-signal path, such as `/v1/traces`, on delivery, unless `traces.endpoint_url` is set.

header_names: array of string



Names of the registered request headers. Header values are write-only and are never returned.



state: [BetaTelemetryDestinationState](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_state)



Whether the destination receives deliveries.

One of the following:



BetaTelemetryDestinationStateEnabled object{ type: "enabled" }



The telemetry destination receives the spans of the workspaces that it covers.

type: "enabled"





BetaTelemetryDestinationStateDisabled object{ type: "disabled", reason }



The API doesn't deliver anything to the telemetry destination.

Spans produced while it is disabled aren't delivered later.

type: "disabled"





reason: [BetaTelemetryDestinationDisabledReason](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_disabled_reason)



Whether a caller or the API disabled the destination and, when the API did, why. Read-only.

One of the following:



traces: [BetaTelemetryDestinationTraces](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_traces) { content_mode, enabled, endpoint_url, max_content_bytes }



The destination's settings for the traces it receives.



content_mode: [BetaTelemetryDestinationContentMode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_content_mode)



What the exported spans contain.

One of the following:

"metadata_only"



The spans contain identifiers, timing, status, token counts, and similar metadata. They don't contain prompt text, completion text, or tool inputs and outputs.



"content"



The spans contain the same metadata as `metadata_only`, plus message and tool content.

An organization with a data-handling restriction, such as under HIPAA, can't choose this mode. The API exports only metadata for such an organization, even to a destination that already has `content`.

enabled: boolean



Whether the destination receives traces. A destination whose `enabled` is false keeps its other settings.



endpoint_url: string or null



The full URL that the API posts traces to, exactly as registered, or `null` if the destination doesn't have one.

When it is `null`, the API posts traces to `endpoint_url` with `/v1/traces` appended.



max_content_bytes: number or null



The most bytes of content that one exported span can contain, or `null` if only the API's maximum applies.

Content means model prompts and responses, and tool inputs and outputs. The API shortens longer content to this size before it delivers the span. A destination whose `content_mode` is `metadata_only` keeps this value. It applies once `content_mode` is `content`.

formatint32



updated_at: string



Time of the last change to the destination's configuration or state. Changes to `delivery_health` don't change it.

An update that sets a header value always changes it, even when the value is the same as before. Adding or removing a single workspace on the destination's list doesn't change it. An update that changes the list does.

formatdate-time



workspaces: [BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspaces](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_workspaces)



Which of the organization's workspaces the destination covers.

One of the following:



BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesAll object{ type: "all" }



The destination covers every workspace of the organization, including the default workspace, archived workspaces, and workspaces created later. It doesn't have a list.

type: "all"





BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesInclude object{ type: "include" }



The destination covers the workspaces on its list, and no others.

type: "include"





BetaTelemetryDestinationWorkspacesExclude object{ type: "exclude" }



The destination covers every workspace of the organization except the workspaces on its list. A workspace created later is covered until it is added to the list.

type: "exclude"



next_page: string or null



Cursor for the next page. Null on the last page.

List Telemetry Destinations

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11' \
    -H "X-Api-Key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "id",
      "created_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
      "delivery_health": {
        "last_error": "last_error",
        "last_error_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
        "last_success_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z"
      },
      "display_name": "display_name",
      "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
      "header_names": [
        "string"
      ],
      "state": {
        "type": "enabled"
      },
      "traces": {
        "content_mode": "metadata_only",
        "enabled": true,
        "endpoint_url": "endpoint_url",
        "max_content_bytes": 0
      },
      "type": "telemetry_destination",
      "updated_at": "2019-12-27T18:11:19.117Z",
      "workspaces": {
        "type": "all"
      }
    }
  ],
  "next_page": "next_page"
}
```

# Test a Telemetry Destination

Copy page



API version 2026-10-21

cURL

POST/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/{destination_id}/test

Send one test span, named `anthropic.test`, to the destination with its registered headers, once and without retries, and report the destination's answer. The response is 200 whether or not the destination answered with a 2xx status: its `result` has the type `success`, or the type `failure` and the reason in `error`. The destination's configuration, `state` and `delivery_health` do not change. A disabled destination can be tested too. Wait 10 seconds between tests of one destination; a request that comes sooner may be answered with status 429.

##### Path parameters

destination_id: string



ID of the destination to test (starts with `tdst_`).

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header.

##### Returns



BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResponse object{ type: "telemetry_destination_test", result }



The result of one test span sent to a destination.

type: "telemetry_destination_test"





result: [BetaTelemetryDestinationTestResult](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/http/beta/organization/telemetry_destinations#beta_telemetry_destination_test_result)



How the test went: `success` when the destination answered with a 2xx status, else `failure` with the reason.

One of the following:



BetaTelemetryDestinationTestSuccess object{ type: "success" }



The destination answered the test span with a 2xx status.

type: "success"





BetaTelemetryDestinationTestFailure object{ type: "failure", error }



The test span was not delivered.

type: "failure"



error: string



A message that describes why the test span was not delivered, including the HTTP status code when the destination returned one. Examples: `HTTP error (status 403)`, `timeout`, `TLS failure`. It has the same form as the destination's `delivery_health.last_error` and never contains the destination's response body, any header value, a network address, or TLS details.

Test a Telemetry Destination

cURL



```python
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/$DESTINATION_ID/test \
    -X POST \
    -H 'anthropic-version: 2026-10-21' \
    -H 'anthropic-beta: telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
```

Response 200



```python
{
  "result": {
    "type": "success"
  },
  "type": "telemetry_destination_test"
}
```

# Update a Telemetry Destination

Copy page



API version 2026-10-21

cURL

POST/v1/organizations/telemetry_destinations/{destination_id}

Change a telemetry destination's settings, its state, or which workspaces it covers.

Send at least one field. Omitted fields keep their stored values, except the registered headers, which a change of the endpoint's hostname or port removes. Only `display_name`, `traces`, `traces.endpoint_url`, `traces.content_mode`, `traces.max_content_bytes`, and individual `headers` values accept `null`.

If another request changes the destination while the update runs, the API returns a 409 `conflict_error`. Read the destination again, then retry the update.

See the [OpenTelemetry export guide](../Other/manage-claude-opentelemetry.md#delivery-and-health) to learn more about changing a destination.

##### Path parameters

destination_id: string



ID of the destination (`tdst_...`).

##### Headers



"anthropic-version": optional string



The version of the Claude API you want to use.

Read more about versioning and our version history [here](../Endpoints/versioning.md).



"anthropic-beta": optional array of [AnthropicBeta](../Endpoints/platform-claude-com-http-beta.md#anthropic_beta)



This endpoint is in beta: requests must send `telemetry-destinations-2026-08-11` in this header.

One of the following:

string



"message-batches-2024-09-24"



"computer-use-2024-10-22"


